items.title: fix: fold SQL table stubs across files and bind schema-qualified names (#4653)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4653. A SQL table got one node per file that read it. A schema-qualified read like `dbo.Customers` never bound to the `CREATE TABLE` in another file, and a plain read like `Invoices` bound to a Python class of the same name.

There were three causes, all in the cross-file pass in `extract()`:

1. Stubs with the same id and no `source_file` are salted apart by `origin_file` in `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`. So each file gets its own `dbo.Orders`.
2. `_is_type_like_definition` rejects any label with a `.`. A SQL table is `schema.name`, so `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` never binds `dbo.Customers` to its definition.
3. `.sql` is not in `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT`, so the cross-language guard treats SQL as unknown and lets the Python class win.

This PR fixes all three in that pass. It doesn't touch the SQL extractor:

```diff
 _LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT
+  ".sql": "sql"

 _is_type_like_definition(node)
-  dotted label -> not a definition
+  dotted label -> not a definition, unless the node comes from a .sql file

 _rewire_unique_stub_nodes
   remap each stub to its unique definition
+  for each stub from a .sql file
+    drop the remap if the definition is in another language
+    if it binds to nothing, group it by _norm_ident(label)
+  fold each group into its smallest id (so file order doesn't matter)
```

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro):

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  dbo_customers                      (a stub, not the table)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (a second dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  app_models_invoices                (the Python class)
```

**After:**

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  tables_customers_dbo_customers     (the CREATE TABLE)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (one dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  invoices                           (a SQL stub)
```

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Each SQL table is one node across the project. A read binds to the `CREATE TABLE` when exactly one file defines it, and never to a definition in another language.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Per-file extraction doesn't change, so the AST cache needs no bump. A revert brings back the per-file stubs on the next build.

**Blast Radius:** SQL nodes, and any edge between SQL and another language. On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336 `.sql` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 739 | 645 |
| table-like nodes | 172 | 79 |
| tables split across several nodes | 25 | 0 |
| non-`contains` edges | 146 | 146 |
| time (median of 3) | 5.5 s | 5.4 s |

`application.cities` goes from 7 nodes to 1, and `application.deliverymethods` from 10 to 1. 94 stub ids go away and none are added.

- **Other languages:** with `.sql` in the families, a call or reference between SQL and another language is no longer a candidate in `_cross_language_candidate`, the function-merge guard, or the cross-file call loop. No test depended on that.
- **Dotted labels in C#, Elixir and Julia:** the fixtures (`Demo.ViewModels`, `MyApp.Accounts.User`, `Base.Threads`) give the same nodes and edges, by sha256, on v8 and on this PR.
- **Saved graphs:** I built wwi-ssdt with v8, then ran this PR in the same folder. `graph.json` has 0 dangling edges and none of the 94 old stub ids. The same holds after editing a view and running `graphify update .` again.

**Limitations**

- **Bracket names:** a stub from `[dbo].[Orders]` and one from `dbo.Orders` fold only after #4649, because on v8 the parser's label is `dbo].[Orders`. A bracketed `CREATE TABLE` does bind (covered by a test).
- **Unqualified names:** `Orders` and `dbo.Orders` stay two tables. The default schema isn't known.
- **Two definitions:** when two files both `CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders`, reads go to one shared stub, not to either definition.
- **Old stub ids:** nothing maps an old per-file stub id to the merged node. A saved semantic edge that points at an old id won't follow it.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_sql_cross_file_tables.py` run `extract()` on small projects and compare node ids and `reads_from` targets. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| an undefined table read from two files is one node (`dbo.Orders`, `Orders`) | fail, fail | pass |
| reads bind to a table defined in another file (`dbo.Orders`) | fail | pass |
| reads bind to a table defined in another file (`Orders`) | pass | pass |
| `[dbo].[Orders]` defined, `dbo.Orders` read in another file | fail | pass |
| a SQL read of `Orders` doesn't bind to a Python `class Orders` | fail | pass |
| guard: a same-file definition still binds | pass | pass |
| guard: `dbo.Orders` and `sales.Orders` stay two tables | pass | pass |

```text

pytest tests/test_sql_cross_file_tables.py (this branch)    -> 8 passed
pytest test_multilang.py test_pg_introspect.py test_extract.py test_ejs_extractor.py -> 463 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)               -> 8479 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check (changed files)                                  -> All checks passed
```

Running `extract()` with the file list reversed gives the same ids. With three files in all 6 orders, the merged node is always `a_sql_dbo_orders`.

items.title: fix(sql): end the statement at GO batch separators (#4651)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

labels.name: needs:title
labels.description: PR title should follow the conventional-commit format

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4651. In a T-SQL script, a `GO` line with no `;` before it hid every statement after it. Those tables and views got no node, and their edges were lost or attached to the wrong node.

`GO` is a command for sqlcmd and SSMS, not SQL. tree-sitter-sql reads it as an identifier, so the statement doesn't end there, and the parser puts `GO` and the rest of the file in one ERROR node.

This PR ends the statement at each `GO` line before parsing:

```diff
 extract_sql
   source = file bytes
+  for each GO [n] line found on the masked text (comments and strings blanked)
+    skip it if a `,` comes right before it, or a `,` or `)` right after it (a column named go)
+    replace `GO` with `;` plus spaces (same length, so byte offsets and line numbers don't move)
   tree = parser.parse(source)
```

A keyword before the line doesn't make it a column. `SET NOCOUNT ON` / `GO` is a real separator, and SSMS writes one before every object.

**Before** (v8):

```sql
SET NOCOUNT ON
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Customers (Id INT PRIMARY KEY)
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders (Id INT, CustomerId INT REFERENCES dbo.Customers(Id))
GO
CREATE VIEW dbo.OpenOrders AS SELECT Id FROM dbo.Orders
GO
```

```text
nodes: dbo.Customers, schema.sql
dbo.Customers  references  dbo.Customers
```

**After:**

```text
nodes: dbo.Customers, dbo.OpenOrders, dbo.Orders, schema.sql
dbo.Orders      references  dbo.Customers
dbo.OpenOrders  reads_from  dbo.Orders
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Each statement between `GO` lines is parsed as its own statement, with or without a `;`. A `GO` inside a comment or string, or a column named `go`, doesn't end a statement.

items.title: fix(sql): strip T-SQL brackets and add reads_from/writes_to edges for procedures (#4635)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4635. On a T-SQL project the SQL graph was close to empty:

1. Bracket names were mangled. `[dbo].[Country]` got the label `dbo].[Country`, and it never matched `dbo.Country`.
2. Stored procedures had no `reads_from` edges, in any dialect.
3. `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`MERGE` made no edge.

Both come from the grammar. tree-sitter-sql 0.3.11 has no T-SQL bracket identifiers: the outer `[` and `]` become ERROR tokens, and the name it keeps is `dbo].[Country`. It also has no `create_procedure` node at all, so the `create_procedure` branch in `sql.py` never runs. Even `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS SELECT a FROM t1;` lands in an ERROR node. The regex recovery then adds the procedure node, and nothing adds its edges. Without `;` between statements, the grammar also merges the body, so the tree has no `insert` or `update` node to read.

So this PR reads procedure bodies as text, not from the tree:

```diff
 extract_sql
   labels and lookup keys
+    strip [ ] from each name part: [dbo].[Orders] -> dbo.Orders, [a]]b] -> a]b
   routine recovery (_ROUTINE_RECOVERY_RX, when the parse has errors)
     add routine node
+    body = after its name, up to the next CREATE/ALTER line, a GO line, or EOF
+    scan the body on the masked text (comments and strings blanked)
+      FROM / JOIN                                          -> reads_from
+      INSERT [INTO] / UPDATE / DELETE [FROM] / MERGE [INTO] / SELECT ... INTO -> writes_to
+      UPDATE o ... FROM dbo.Orders o                        -> alias resolves to dbo.Orders
+      skip CTE names, @variables, #temp/##temp, table-valued function calls
+    one edge per (routine, relation, table)
```

Ids don't change: `_make_id` already dropped the brackets, so only labels and in-file matching were wrong. Double-quoted names (`"dbo"."V"`) keep their labels. Routines the tree parses cleanly (PostgreSQL `$$` functions) keep their tree-based edges and aren't scanned a second time.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8, `graphify update .`):

```text
dbo].[Country reads_from dbo].[tbl_Country
(3 procedures: contains only)
```

**After:**

```text
dbo.Country               reads_from  dbo.tbl_Country
dbo.GetOrderTotal()       reads_from  dbo.Orders
dbo.GetOrderTotal()       reads_from  dbo.Payments
dbo.GetOrderTotalPlain()  reads_from  dbo.Orders
dbo.GetOrderTotalPlain()  reads_from  dbo.Payments
dbo.AddPayment()          writes_to   dbo.Orders
dbo.AddPayment()          writes_to   dbo.Payments
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

`writes_to` is a new relation. Nothing outside `sql.py` lists relation names, so it needs no registration.

## Verification & Invariants

A procedure has a `reads_from` edge to each table it reads and a `writes_to` edge to each table it writes, and none to aliases, variables, temp tables, CTEs, or names in comments and strings. A name gets the same label and key with or without brackets.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Ids are unchanged. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes 20 -> 21 so cached `.sql` extractions re-run, and a revert re-runs them again. #4572 and #4573 also take 21, so whichever lands second needs 22.

**Blast Radius:** SQL only. On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336 `.sql` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 739 | 1011 |
| non-`contains` edges | 146 | 465 |
| time (median of 3) | 5.7 s | 5.8 s |

- **Removed:** no v8 edge. The edges that show as removed in a text diff are the same edges with bracket-free labels.
- **Added:** 190 `reads_from` and 129 `writes_to`. All 319 were checked against the source: 314 have the keyword right before the table name, and 5 are `UPDATE sih ... FROM Warehouse.StockItemHoldings AS sih` alias updates.
- **False positives:** none among the 61 distinct targets. 13 are `sys.*` catalog views, which are real references. 36 edges sit on routines that only exist because of the mask's known multi-line-string hole (`Configuration_*InMemory.sql` build procedures inside multi-line `N'...'` strings).
- **Existing tests:** 10 assertions in `test_multilang.py` change their expected routine label to the bracket-free form (`[dbo].[usp_Real]()` -> `dbo.usp_Real()`). `test_sql_tsql_bracketed_procedure_is_recovered` now filters to routine nodes, since the procedure's tables now appear as stubs.

**Limitations**

- **One node per file for undefined tables.** A table no file defines, referenced from N files, becomes N stub nodes. In the repro that's three `dbo.Orders` nodes. v8 does the same. Answering "what writes to `dbo.Orders`" across a project needs that fixed. Filed as #<stub-issue>.
- **`GO` without `;`** still swallows the next statement in the tree, so a second `CREATE TABLE` after `GO` is lost. Filed as #<go-issue>.
- When a procedure both reads and writes a table, `graph.json` keeps one edge per pair, so only `writes_to` shows. `extract()` returns both.
- `MERGE ... USING src` records no read. `TRUNCATE` and `EXEC` aren't modelled. `BULK INSERT dbo.T` counts as a write.
- A `CREATE`/`ALTER` at the start of a line inside a body (`CREATE INDEX ... ON #t`) ends the body early. `CREATE TABLE #t` and `CREATE TABLE @t` don't.
- Trigger and index labels keep their brackets.
- The `create_procedure` and `fb_proc_or_trigger` branches are dead on this grammar. They're left as they are.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_sql_tsql_procedures.py` run `extract()` or `extract_sql()` on small files, including the issue's four, and assert `(source, relation, target)` triples. None calls a private helper.

|---|---|---|
| T1: `[dbo].[Orders]` and `dbo.Orders` in one file are one table | fail | pass |
| T2: no half-stripped labels; labels are `dbo.Orders`, `dbo.AddPayment()`; `[a]]b]` -> `a]b`; `"dbo"."V"` kept | fail | pass |
| T3: each repro procedure reads its tables | fail | pass |
| T4: plain `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS SELECT ...`, with `(x INT)`, with `@x INT ... BEGIN END` | fail | pass |
| T5: `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `SELECT ... INTO` give `writes_to`; `DELETE FROM` isn't a read | fail | pass |
| T9: `UPDATE o ... FROM dbo.Orders o` writes `dbo.Orders` | fail | pass |
| T10: `#work`, `##shared`, `@ids` are skipped | fail | pass |
| T11: `GO`-separated procedures keep their own tables; comments and strings are ignored | fail | pass |
| guards: aliases, columns, variables, CTEs, two procedures in one file, top-level statements, function and view reads, one edge per triple | pass | pass |

On v8 the guards pass because v8 makes no procedure edges. They catch a fix that attaches too much.

```text
pytest tests/test_sql_tsql_procedures.py (this branch)    -> 33 passed
pytest test_multilang.py test_pg_introspect.py test_extract.py -> 448 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp) -> 8504 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check (changed files)                                 -> All checks passed
```

The cache bump was checked on the repro: a v8 run writes the cache, then this branch with the schema forced back to 20 serves the old labels and the single edge. At 21 it re-extracts and gives the 7 edges above.

items.title: fix(js): resolve ns.fn() calls through namespace imports (#4619)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4619. A call through a namespace import made no `calls` edge:

```ts
import * as ops from './ops'
export function dispatch(n: number) { return ops.submit(n) }   // no dispatch -> submit
```

It failed in both call paths:

- The symbol-resolution pass (`resolution.py`) never recorded `import * as ops`, and kept only bare-identifier callees, so `ops.submit` was dropped. #3517 fixed aliased named imports here and left namespace imports for later.
- The per-file engine saw the member call, then looked `submit` up by bare name in the caller's own file. When that file has its own `submit`, the call bound to it, so the edge pointed at the wrong function. Otherwise the call was parked, and the cross-file loop skips every member call.

The engine now knows which import binds each receiver. The resolution pass resolves `fn` against the module's real exports:

```diff
 engine: member call ns.fn()
+  if ns is bound by `import * as ns from './m'` (corpus file, not shadowed in the caller)
+    skip the same-file bare-name lookup
+    stamp the raw call with (m, "*")
 resolution pass
+  record `import * as ns` as an import fact with imported name "*"
+  turn each stamped call into a use fact `ns.fn`
+  fn = the one export of m named fn (re-export chains, `export { a as b }`, `export * as ns`)
+  no export of that name -> no edge
```

The lookup uses the export table that named imports already use (`exported_candidates`), so it handles renames the same way. Unlike `resolve_exported_origin`, it doesn't fall back to "a symbol with that name exists in the file", so `ns.privateFn()` makes no edge.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8):

```text
calls dispatch() -> helper()
```

**After:**

```text
calls dispatch() -> helper()
calls dispatch() -> submit()
calls dispatch() -> reveal()
calls direct()   -> submit()
```

I chose this after writing the tests first and running four candidates against them:

| | A: resolution pass only | B: engine + new resolver | C: A + class methods + engine guard | D: engine binding + export table (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| issue repro (T1) | 4/4 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| class methods, nested functions, `.tsx`, `.mjs` (T2) | 3/5 | 5/5 | 4/5 | 5/5 |
| through barrels (T3) | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `export { a as b }`: `x.b()` edge, `x.a()` none | pass | fail | pass | pass |
| no edge to an unexported function | fail | fail | fail | pass |
| no edge to a same-named function in the caller's file | fail | pass | pass | pass |
| shadowing, external package, `import type` (T4) | pass | pass | pass | pass |

B rebuilt the export table from graph labels. That lost the renamed name and treated every `contains` child as an export.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A call `ns.fn()` through `import * as ns from './m'` has a `calls` edge to the function `m` exports as `fn`, and to nothing else.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No id changes and no schema bump: JS/TS files skip the per-file AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`), so the next extract gives the new edges, and a revert gives v8 output again.

**Blast Radius:** small. Only JS/TS graphs change, and only around namespace imports. On a 2876-file TypeScript project, 12 edges were added and 7 removed out of 15567, and I checked each against the source:

- **Removed:** 7 calls like `ops.add()` inside a class method `add()`, which v8 bound to the class's own `.add()`.
- **Added:** those 7 calls, plus `ops.list()` and `ops.wakeNow()`, now point at `service/ops.ts`. 3 more are calls inside `it(...)` callbacks, through an `export *` barrel.

Extraction took 37.7 s, against 38.6 s on v8 (median of 3).

**Limitations**

- A top-level `ns.fn()` statement, outside any function, still makes no edge, the same as a bare call. `test_ts_import_require.py` pins the edges of that case.
- `ops.a.b()` and `const f = ops.submit; f()` still make no edge. `new ops.K()` and `const { submit } = ops; submit()` now do. All four are `xfail(strict=False)`, because their wanted behaviour isn't decided.
- Only relative imports resolve, the same as other JS imports here (`_resolve_js_module_path`). `tsconfig` path aliases and Vue/Svelte callers are untested.
- The `"*"` import fact goes into the shared alias table. `"*"` is never an export name, so a bare `ops()` resolves to nothing.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_js_exported_fn_call_resolution.py`, next to the #3346 tests. Each one runs `extract()` on a small project and asserts `(caller, callee, callee file)` edges. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| T1: issue repro, each of the 3 namespace edges | fail | pass |
| T1: `dispatch -> helper` | pass | pass |
| T2: arrow (`.js`), class method, nested function, `.tsx`, `.mjs` | fail | pass |

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4588. Stacked on #4573, so only the last two commits are new: 467f15ba (tests) and 25d072bc (fix).

The VB resolver dropped calls made through a field, through `Me.field`, and inside `With` blocks:

```vb
Private _repo As Repository        ' F1-F5
_repo.Save()                       ' no edge
Me._repo.Save()                    ' no edge
With _repo
    .Load()                        ' no edge
End With
```

Fields had no declared type, so a field receiver hid the call and nothing replaced it.

```diff
 resolve(call)
   locals / parameters
+  field of the caller's type (all partial files), then VB bases nearest first
+    declared type known and unique -> member of that type, INFERRED 0.85
+    untyped / external / ambiguous -> no edge (still hides a same-named type)
   type or Module named by the receiver

 walk(method body)
+  With target stack: `.M()` -> call on the innermost target
+    name / Me.name -> resolved like name.M()
+    New T()        -> typed receiver T
+    anything else  -> no edge
```

- Only `As T` and `As New T()` give a field a type. `Private x = New T()` is `Object` to the compiler, because Option Infer doesn't apply to fields.
- The field's type is resolved with the declaring file's namespace and imports.
- `Me.f`, `MyClass.f` and `OwnType.f` resolve like `f`.
- A typed local or field of an interface type binds to the interface member, as the compiler does.
- VB→C# edges keep the `_vbnet_resolved` marker from #4573.
- `watch.py` forwards `declared_type` and `imports`. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 21 → 22.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4570. In a VB.NET project, `calls` edges appeared only when the caller and the callee were in the same file.

For each invocation, `extract_vbnet` picks the type that owns the target. An unqualified call or a `Me` call gets the caller's own type. A qualified call is looked up in `owner_by_short`, which only holds types declared in that file. Anything else (a Module in another file, a local variable, a C# type) got `target_owner = None` and was dropped: no edge and no raw call, so no resolver could see it. The only VB resolver, `resolve_vbnet_partial_calls`, matches `(owner, name, arity)` for `Partial` types. The shared name pass skips VB calls because they are marked as member calls.

| Call in `Caller.vb` | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `LogIt("x")`, a Module Sub in another file | raw call with owner `Caller`, no edge | `LogIt` in `Helpers.vb`, EXTRACTED |
| `Helpers.LogIt("x")`, Module in another file | dropped | EXTRACTED |
| `Dim w As New Worker()` then `w.Save()` | dropped | `Worker.Save`, INFERRED |
| `CsRules.IsLocked(1)`, a C# static | dropped | EXTRACTED |
| `.Save()` inside `With w` | **wrong edge** to the caller's own `Save` | no edge |
| `handler(1)`, `handler` a local `Action(Of Integer)` | **wrong edge** to a `handler` method | no edge |

The extractor now emits a raw call for every invocation, with the written receiver, its kind (`none`, `me`, `mybase`, `name`, `local`), the declared type of a local or parameter, the caller's namespace, the file's `Imports` and the caller's nested types. The raw calls keep `is_member_call`, so the shared name pass still never sees them. `resolve_vbnet_calls` replaces the partial-type resolver (the old name stays as an alias and as the registry name) and follows VB's lookup order:

```text
resolve(call)
  unqualified / Me
    nearest of own type, then in-corpus bases, that declares the name -> it decides, at any arity
    a field, property or event with the name -> no edge
    else Modules in scope (same, enclosing, global or imported namespace) with that member
      exactly one Module, exactly one arity match -> edge, else none
  MyBase                -> the base chain only
  local / parameter     -> its declared type, then member lookup          (INFERRED)
  Type.M() / Module.M() -> a field or nested type of that name hides it
                           else the type unique in scope, VB or C#, then member lookup
  a VB target must accept the arity; a C# target must be the only method of that name
  a caller whose base chain leaves the corpus -> INFERRED, context external_base_may_hide
```

Only a unique match makes an edge. Nothing falls back to a name match across the corpus.

I checked every rule against the compiler before writing it. I used dotnet SDK 8.0 in a container, offline, with small VB projects that print which method ran:

| Case | Compiler |
|---|---|
| unqualified call, Module in another file, same namespace | binds the Module |
| Module in another namespace, no `Imports` | BC30451 |
| with `Imports`, or Module in an enclosing namespace | binds the Module |
| caller's class or its base declares `LogIt` (any arity) | binds the class method, or BC30455 |
| two Modules declare `LogIt`, even at different arities | BC30562 |
| field, property, delegate field or nested type with the name | hides the Module |
| two `Helpers` in namespaces the caller doesn't import | BC30451 |
| `As New Worker()`, `As Worker = New Worker()`, `Dim w = New Worker()` | `Worker.Save` |
| `CsRules.IsLocked(1)` and `csrules.islocked(1)` from VB | the C# method |
| `.Save()` in `With w` | `w.Save` |
| `handler(1)`, `handler` a local delegate | the delegate |

`watch.py` now forwards `owner`, `full_name`, `accepted_arities` and `namespace` to the context nodes of unchanged files (#2406). Without them, an unchanged `Helpers.vb` reached the resolver with no owner. This has two side effects: the existing partial-type resolver now works on incremental rebuilds too, and `_resolve_csharp_qualified_calls` binds the same as a full build on an incremental rebuild. With `Svc` in both `Alpha` and `Beta` and a caller with `using Beta`, v8 bound an incremental rebuild to `Alpha.Svc.Save`, and now binds `Beta.Svc.Save`. Only the VB resolver and that C# resolver read `metadata.namespace`.

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18. #4567 and #4572 bump the same line from 17 to 18, so whichever lands later needs 19.

**Before** (the issue's repro, `extract --code-only --force`):

```text
A_SameFileSelf -> B_Target()   EXTRACTED
.G_CsToVb      -> LogIt()      EXTRACTED
```

**After:**

```text
A_SameFileSelf      -> B_Target()    EXTRACTED
C_UnqualifiedModule -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
D_QualifiedModule   -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
E_TypedLocal        -> Save()        INFERRED   call
F_CsStatic          -> .IsLocked()   EXTRACTED  call
.G_CsToVb           -> LogIt()       EXTRACTED  call
```

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A VB.NET call gets a `calls` edge exactly when the VB compiler's lookup gives one target in the corpus, and never to a target the compiler would not pick.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. New raw-call fields, a resolver, four metadata keys forwarded in `watch.py`, and a cache schema bump. No id, graph format or manifest change. Reverting restores v8 output after one re-extract.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. VB.NET graphs gain many `calls` edges, so `affected`, `path`, `explain`, god nodes and communities change for VB projects. Two kinds of wrong v8 edges go away (`With` blocks, local delegates). C# changes only on incremental rebuilds, where it now matches a full build. | edge confidence for each form (×4) | fail | pass |
| inherited method reached | fail | pass |
| lowercase VB call reaches a C# method | fail | pass |

| class method hides the Module at any arity | pass | pass |
| two Modules with the same name give no edge (×2) | pass | pass |
| `As Object` receiver binds to nothing | pass | pass |
| never binds a same-named Python function | pass | pass |

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4569. Each package.json dependency produced two nodes labelled `react` with no edge between them:

- the manifest entry `<stem>_dependencies_react` (type code, carries the version-range line), reached through `dependencies --contains-->`;
- the ref node `ref_react` (type concept), reached through `package.json --imports-->`. Code imports (`import React from "react"`) resolve here.

5711e9d2 (#1764 follow-up) moved the `imports` edge from `key_nid` to `file_nid` so it would stop reading as `react --imports--> react`. That edge was the only link between the two nodes. On v8 the manifest entry is 4 hops from the code that imports the package, the two land in different communities, `explain react` exits 3 ("Ambiguous: 'react' matches 2 nodes in package.json"), and `affected react` prints "No unique node match".

The manifest entry now has a `declares` edge to the ref node and is labelled `name@range`:

```diff
 elif parent_key in _DEP_KEYS and val_text.strip():
     dep_nid = _make_id("ref", key)
     add_node(dep_nid, key, line, file_type="concept")
     add_edge(file_nid, dep_nid, "imports", line, context="import")
+    add_edge(key_nid, dep_nid, "declares", line)
+    version = one line of val_text, capped at 40 chars ("...")
+    relabel key_nid to f"{key}@{version}"   # only if its source_location is this line
```

The ref node keeps the bare name that imports resolve to, so the two nodes no longer share a label: no `react -> react` edge, and `react` resolves to one node. A blank range (`"   "`) now behaves like `""`: bare label, no ref, no edge. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18.

The relabel checks `source_location` because a key node id carries only the immediate parent key. In a v2 lockfile, `dependencies.semver` under two `node_modules/*` entries mints one node; `add_node` keeps the first, so relabelling every pair would put the later range on the first line (4 of 44 relabelled nodes on a 340-package lockfile).

**Before** (the issue's package.json):

```text
dependencies --contains--> react [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
```

**After:**

```text
dependencies --contains--> react@^19.0.0 [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
react@^19.0.0 --declares--> react [concept]
```

I chose this after writing tests for the wanted behaviour and running four candidates against them:

| | A: `declares` edge | A2: `references` edge | B: no key node | C: edge + `name@range` (this PR) |

| entry connected to importing code | yes | yes | yes | yes |

| existing tests pass | yes | yes | no (`test_extract_json_nested_contains`) | yes |

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4563. When the hook's interpreter probes 1 to 4 all miss, its last resort tried `python3` before `python`. On Windows 10/11, `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`, because python.org's installer ships `python.exe` but no `python3.exe`. Running the alias opens a console window for about 1.1 s and exits 9009. The hook then falls through to the real `python`, so it works, but every commit, checkout and merge flashes a window and blocks before the detached rebuild starts.

The last resort is reached when the pinned interpreter, `.graphify_python`, the launcher and the uv-tools scan all miss: a removed venv, graphify moved to another env, or a GUI client with a minimal PATH.

Under Git for Windows the last resort now tries `python` first. The Windows check is the one `hooks.py` already uses for its pipe-handle handling.

```diff
 # Last resort: try python3 / python (works for system/venv installs on PATH).
+# Under Git for Windows `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias
+# ... Try `python` first there (#4563).
 if [ -z "$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON" ]; then
-    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python3"
-    elif command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && python -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python"
+    if [ -n "${WINDIR:-}" ] || [ -n "${MSYSTEM:-}" ]; then
+        _GFY_FIRST="python"; _GFY_SECOND="python3"
+    else
```

items.title: fix(rust): name a use rooted at a sibling mod so it reaches its declaration (#4564)

labels.name: contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4564. A Rust `use` rooted at a child module declared beside it, such as `pub use item::Invoice;` next to `mod item;`, left its `imports_from` edge dangling. Build then minted an `external` stub `invoice`, and `affected` and `explain` tied on it.

The #4439 fix lends `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` a temporary node for every edge that carries `_rust_use_name`. `name_use` sets that only when the path's first segment is `crate`, `self` or `super`, so that `use serde::Serialize` never lands on a corpus `Serialize` (5faa05c8). `item::Invoice` starts with `item`, which looks the same as `serde::` to that check, so it got no lent node.

Rust settles which one a first segment means. A `mod` declared in the same scope shadows a crate of the same name, and only a leading `::` reaches the crate. Checked with `cargo check` on rustc 1.95.0, using a stand-in `serde` crate:

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| `mod serde { … }` + `use serde::Serialize;`, same scope | E0432 |
| `mod serde;` (file module) + `use serde::Serialize;` | E0432 |
| `mod serde` + `use ::serde::Serialize;` | compiles, reaches the crate |
| top-level `mod serde` + `mod tests { use serde::Serialize; }` | compiles, reaches the crate |

So the rule is exact: a first segment that names a sibling `mod_item` is this crate's, unless the path starts with `::`.

```diff
 use_declaration
+  scope_mods = names of mod_item siblings of this use     # either order; an inline mod is its own scope
   name_use(written, path)
-    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+       or (first segment in scope_mods and path does not start with "::")
       edge._rust_use_name = written
```

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18, so a cached 0.9.92 result without the name is not served.

**Before** (the issue's four files, `extract --code-only --cargo --force`, `cluster-only`):

```text
graph.json   NODE invoice  type=external  source_file=''
             EDGE src_model -> invoice
affected Invoice   No unique node match for Invoice                      (exit 0)
explain Invoice    Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.   (exit 3)
```

**After:**

```text
graph.json   EDGE src_model -> src_model_item_invoice    (no external node)
affected Invoice   Affected nodes for Invoice …
explain Invoice    Node: Invoice  ID: src_model_item_invoice  Source: src/model/item.rs L1
```

**Door:** two-way. One extra condition in `name_use` and a cache schema bump. No graph format, id or manifest change. Reverting restores v8 behaviour. The schema bump costs one re-extract of cached Rust files on the next forced run.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only Rust `use` edges rooted at a sibling `mod` change, and only from a dangling stub to the real declaration. `use` paths rooted at `crate`, `self`, `super`, `::` or an outside crate behave as on v8. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, not only Rust entries, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- An incremental `graphify extract` (no `--force`) skips a file whose content hash matches `manifest.json` before it reads the AST cache (`detect_incremental`). The schema bump never reaches those files, so an existing graph keeps the stub until `--force` or an edit to the file. items.title: fix(extract): let the model acknowledge empty files so they don't arm the shrink guard (#4547)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4547. A file the model read and found empty (a `robots.txt`, an HTML shell, a short compose file) failed `graphify extract` on every run, the same way a file the model skipped does.

A file sent for semantic extraction counts as covered only if a returned node has it as `source_file`. Zero nodes puts it in `uncovered_files`, which sets `_extraction_incomplete`. That turns off `force`, so any run where the graph shrinks is refused and exits non-zero. The response format has only `nodes`, `edges` and `hyperedges`, so the model has no way to say "read it, nothing here." A retry sends the same file and gets the same answer.

A file the model read and found empty also failed a second way. A chunk holding only that file got an empty response, which `_response_is_hollow` treats as hollow. It was retried at 2 s and 8 s, then marked partial, which also arms the guard.

What changes, per file sent:

| Model's response for the file | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | covered | covered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities: 0` | uncovered, guard armed | `empty_files`, guard not armed |
| no nodes, not listed | uncovered | uncovered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities > 0` | uncovered | uncovered |
| no `files` key at all | uncovered | uncovered |
| in a truncated or hollow chunk | partial | partial, whatever it says |

```diff
 _EXTRACTION_SYSTEM schema
-{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0}
+{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"files":[{"path":"relative/path","entities":0}],...}

 _extract_with_adaptive_retry
   result = extract_files_direct(chunk)
+  _take_acks(result)        # keep 0-entity acks for paths in THIS chunk -> _empty_files
+                            # acks name only some files and no items -> hollow, normal retry

 _response_is_hollow
-  return not nodes and not edges and not hyperedges
+  no items and every acknowledged file has entities == 0 -> not hollow

 extract_corpus_parallel
-  uncovered = dispatched - covered
+  empty_files = (dispatched - covered) & acked_empty - partial
+  uncovered   = dispatched - covered - empty_files
```

The CLI also writes the full uncovered list to `graphify-out/uncovered_files.txt`, with paths relative to the corpus root, and removes a stale copy at the start of the next extract. Before this, the warning named five files and "+N more", and the rest were only in memory. The llm.py warning no longer says a re-run will retry the files. They are re-sent every run, but with the same `--token-budget` the model usually skips the same ones.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Only a file the model left out, or one from a truncated or hollow chunk, arms the shrink guard. A file the model read and acknowledged as empty does not.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. `files` is optional and is read only by the coverage check. It is popped before anything reaches the cache or `graph.json`. A response without it behaves exactly as on v8. Reverting the commit restores the old behaviour, and no stored data needs migrating.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. Every semantic extraction prompt gains the `files` rule, so each response gets slightly longer (one short entry per file). Runs that failed only because of empty files now write the graph. The guard now trusts a model's 0 for a file that comes back with no nodes.

**Limitations**

items.body:
Fixes #4508. A community relabelled only by case keeps its wiki article on case-insensitive filesystems. ## Summary On APFS (macOS) and NTFS (Windows), `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are one file. When a community's label changes from `groups` to `Groups`, the export writes into the existing entry, and the entry keeps its old case. The end-of-run orphan sweep compared names case-sensitively, so it deleted the page the run had just written. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before B1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> B2{"sweep: 'groups.md' in produced?"} B2 -- "no (case differs)" --> B3["unlink groups.md
index.md links to missing file"] end subgraph After A1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> A2{"sweep: same device+inode
as a produced page?"} A2 -- yes --> A3["keep, rename to Groups.md"] A2 -- no --> A4["unlink stale page"] end ``` The sweep now matches files by identity (device and inode) instead of by name. A page this run wrote is kept, and its entry is renamed to the produced case. A stale page that is a separate file is still removed. Case-folding the names was the other option in the issue. It was rejected because on Linux `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are two real files, so folding would keep a stale page. Changed: `graphify/wiki.py` (the sweep block plus a `_file_id` helper, 21 lines added, 1 removed). New: `tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py` (2 tests). ## Evidence - **Before:** `to_wiki` relabel `groups` → `Groups` on upstream `v8`: `['Groups.md', 'index.md', 'other.md']`, but `Groups.md` is not a readable file. `index.md` links to it. The test `test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs` fails with `AssertionError` on `Groups.md` `is_file()`. - **After:** same run on this branch: `Groups.md` is readable and `index.md` links to it. Test passes. ```text upstream v8 test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs FAILED test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed this branch test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs passed test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed wiki suites (test_wiki, link_filename_parity, idempotent_writes, path_length) 70 passed, 3 skipped full suite (tests/) 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ruff check graphify/wiki.py + new test All checks passed ``` The case-insensitive test simulates APFS and NTFS with a symlink, because the test machine runs Linux. The test helper `_case_insensitive_write` documents this. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. The change touches only the orphan sweep. No file format, schema or cache key changes. Reverting restores the name-based sweep. **Blast radius:** wiki export (`to_wiki`). It runs on every `graphify` export that writes a wiki. Output is unchanged unless a case-only relabel happens. The sweep now calls `stat` on each `*.md` in the wiki folder, which is one extra call per page. A stat failure on a dangling symlink still removes the link as before. ## What does this PR do? Fixes #4508. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a relabel that changes only case used to delete the new article and leave `index.md` pointing at it. The sweep now keeps any page this run wrote, even when its on-disk name has the old case, and renames the entry to the new case. - Single-case runs are unchanged. Each produced page still gets one file. - A stale page that is a different file is still removed on every platform. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [x] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants Invariant: after an export, every page `index.md` links to exists, and the sweep never deletes a page the run wrote. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** that fails on upstream `v8` and passes here. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. ## How was this tested? ```text PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4508 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/... -q tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py -> 2 passed (this branch); 1 failed, 1 passed (upstream v8) full suite: 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ``` ## Limitations - Not run on a real APFS or NTFS volume. labels.name: contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4512.

In a merged multi-repo graph, two nodes can share a label and a repo-relative `source_file`, for example `web/dup.py` and `ml/dup.py`. Both appear as `dup.py`. The same-file check used the bare `source_file`, so the two nodes counted as one file. `explain` and `path` then refused with "matches 2 nodes in dup.py", listed bare `L1` lines, and gave a hint that could not tell the candidates apart.

This PR makes a file the pair (repo, source_file). The refusal names each candidate's file with its repo, and when the same path exists in more than one repo, the hint says so and asks for the full node id.

```text
_rivals_across_files(tier)
  before: key = source_file           -> web/dup.py and ml/dup.py collapse to "dup.py"
  after:  key = (repo, source_file)   -> two files, cross-file branch

_ambiguity_message(...)
  repos differ        -> list "web/dup.py", "ml/dup.py"
  same path, 2 repos  -> hint: "the same path exists in more than one repo ..."
  otherwise           -> unchanged
```

- A repo is shown in the refusal only when the candidates span more than one repo.
- Single-repo graphs (no `repo` attribute) keep the old wording.
- Same-file duplicates keep the old same-file branch.

items.title: fix(hooks): rebuild after cherry-pick, rebase and pull --rebase (#4490)

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4490. After a clean `git cherry-pick`, a `git rebase` or a `git pull --rebase`, the hooks never launched a rebuild, so `graph.json` described the old code until the next plain commit.

There are two causes:
- **Cherry-pick.** `post-commit` exited on `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, which git leaves on disk while the hook runs. This is the same trap as `MERGE_HEAD` in #4463.
- **Rebase.** `post-commit` and `post-checkout` skip while `rebase-merge/` exists, and no hook rebuilt at the end.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8 `10130e79`):

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 0 rebuilds
git rebase main        -> 0 rebuilds
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

**After:**

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 1 rebuild
git rebase main        -> 1 rebuild
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

```text
post-commit:
  drop the CHERRY_PICK_HEAD exit
  if sequencer/todo exists and its first line is the commit just made:
    more than one step left  -> skip (mid range pick or revert)
    last step                -> CHANGED = diff sequencer/head..HEAD   (one rebuild covers the range)
  else: a stale sequencer/ (left by git reset --hard) is ignored -> normal HEAD~1 rebuild

post-rewrite (new hook):
  $1 = rebase -> launch an unscoped rebuild, like post-merge
  $1 = amend  -> exit (post-commit already rebuilt)
  no rebase-merge check: rebase-merge/ is still on disk when post-rewrite runs
```

Why only the last step rebuilds: if `graphify-out/graph.json` is tracked, a rebuild between picks rewrites it, and git then refuses a later pick that touches it (`Your local changes ... would be overwritten by merge: graphify-out/graph.json`). Just dropping the `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` check hit exactly that.

```diff
 graphify/hooks.py
   _HOOK_SCRIPT (post-commit)
-    [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
+    sequencer/todo check: skip mid-sequence, last step diffs from sequencer/head,
+    stale sequencer/ ignored
+  _REWRITE_SCRIPT (new), _REWRITE_HOOK_MARKER / _END
   install / uninstall / status
+    post-rewrite, same append/preserve handling as the other hooks
 graphify/__main__.py
   hook install help line names post-rewrite
```

### Existing tests this PR changes

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hooks_reuse_git_dir_from_env` | every script in `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` must contain `GIT_DIR=${GIT_DIR:-` | required only when the script reads `$GIT_DIR` | the new post-rewrite hook never reads `$GIT_DIR`; adding an unused line would be dead code |
| `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` parametrize list | 3 hooks | adds `post-rewrite` | the nohup, detach, worker-cap and quote-safety tests now cover the new hook too |

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Every git operation that changes the tree launches one rebuild when it finishes, and no hook rebuilds in the middle of a pick, revert or rebase sequence.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Shell hook scripts and one new hook file. No schema, cache or file-format change.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. This changes when the hooks launch a rebuild, not what a rebuild does:
- A clean cherry-pick, a rebase and `pull --rebase` now rebuild once.
- A range pick or revert rebuilds once at the end. A revert range used to rebuild after every step, with the same final graph.
- Plain commits, amends, checkouts and merges behave as before.
- `graphify hook install` now also writes `.git/hooks/post-rewrite`, appending to a user's existing one like the other hooks. `GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1` turns it off.

**Limitations**

- `--skip` on the last pick and `--quit` still leave the graph stale, as on v8. git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.
- If you edit the commit message while resolving a pick, or revert a `Revert "..."` commit, the todo line no longer matches HEAD. That step is then treated as a stale sequencer and rebuilds mid-sequence. It never skips a rebuild. This comes from reading the logic, not a test.

- This PR doesn't touch `post-merge`. #4476 fixes that, and the two merge cleanly in either order. Merged together, the hook tests give 184 passed.

New `tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py` runs real git operations against the installed hooks and counts rebuild launches. Four of its tests run a real build and check the graph contents. Against v8's hooks it gives 8 failed and 4 passed. The 4 that pass are behaviours v8 already gets right: the plain-commit control, amend, the tracked-graph sequence, and the abandoned pick. `tests/test_hooks.py` adds install, uninstall, status and append/preserve tests for post-rewrite. It also adds hook-level tests for the sequencer logic: skip mid-sequence, the diff from `sequencer/head` covering every picked file, and the stale-todo cases.

items.title: fix(hooks): drop MERGE_HEAD guard from post-merge so real merges rebuild (#4463)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4463. The post-merge hook never rebuilt after a merge that makes a merge commit (`--no-ff`, diverged branches, `git pull`). Only fast-forward merges rebuilt.

`_MERGE_SCRIPT` exits early if `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists. On git 2.54, MERGE_HEAD is still on disk while post-merge runs, and git deletes it after the hook returns. A fast-forward never writes it, which is why those merges still worked. I reproduced this on Linux with git 2.54.0, so it isn't specific to Windows.

What the hook sees while it runs:

| Merge | MERGE_HEAD during post-merge | v8 hook |
|---|---|---|
| fast-forward | absent | rebuilds |
| `--no-ff` | present | exits |
| diverged branches | present | exits |
| `git pull` (diverged) | present | exits |

So the #2418 cleanup (removing symbols the union merge driver brings back) never ran on a real merge.

**Before** (`sh -x` on the installed hook, `git merge --no-ff feat`):

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ']'
+ exit 0
```

**After:**

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD ']'
...
[graphify] Merge completed - launching background rebuild (log: ...)
```

```diff
 _MERGE_SCRIPT
-# This hook only fires after a merge completed cleanly, so MERGE_HEAD is
-# already gone by the time it runs -- ...
+# git leaves MERGE_HEAD on disk while post-merge runs and deletes it only
+# after the hook returns, so it must not be checked here (#4463). ...
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-merge" ] && exit 0
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-apply" ] && exit 0
-[ -f "$GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD" ] && exit 0
 [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
```

Git only runs post-merge after a successful merge, so the check never protected anything there. The same check in post-commit and post-checkout is unchanged. There it keeps those hooks quiet while a conflicted merge is being resolved.

- [ ] Security fix

Every merge that changes the tree triggers one post-merge rebuild. Hooks still stay quiet mid rebase or cherry-pick.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4461.

Four comment lines inside double-quoted `-c "..."` blocks had backticks. Bash expands backticks inside double quotes, so it ran the text before Python started. This PR drops the backticks, keeps the words, and adds a test that fails on any backtick inside such a block.

### Summary

```diff
 # Part C, in core/core.md:317, core/aider.md:378, core/devin.md:442 (15 generated skills)
-# `graphify update` deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it
+# graphify update deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it

 # --update merge block, in references/shared/update.md:110 (all 14 skills/<host>/references/update.md)
-# Do NOT add `changed` here: with root= passed, prune_set relativizes to the same base
+# Do NOT add changed here: with root= passed, prune_set relativizes to the same base
```

The skills run Python as `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."`. With `graphify` on PATH, bash ran a full `graphify update` in the middle of Part C and pasted its output into the Python source. The first output line landed in the comment. The next lines were pasted into the code, and Part C failed with `SyntaxError`. `.graphify_extract.json` was never written. Without `graphify` on PATH the only sign was `command not found` on stderr, so nobody noticed.

Two commits:
1. `test(skill): no command runs from backticks in -c "..." blocks`: `tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`. On its own it fails 58 cases (29 per check).
2. `fix(skill): drop backticks bash ran inside Part C and the update merge (#4461)`: the 4 fragment lines, the regenerated files, and one `gen.py` line.

### Evidence

- **Test before and after:** unfixed v8 58 failed, 105 passed. After the fix 163 passed. The 58 are 29 files per check: 15 monoliths plus 14 `references/update.md`.
- **Real graphify on PATH** (Part C copied verbatim from `graphify/skill.md:377-417`, a project with a previous build and one edited file, venv `graphify` first on PATH):

  ```text
  before (v8 fe085ced)
    exit 1   SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?
             at "[graphify watch] 3 file(s) not classified ..." (graphify's own stdout)
    graph.json rewritten by the unrequested update (sha prefix e4df2084c90f7f07 -> 70d4be72e1eab745)
    .graphify_extract.json: not written

  after (this branch)
    exit 0   stdout: Merged: 1 nodes, 0 edges (1 AST + 0 semantic)   stderr: empty
    graph.json unchanged (sha prefix fa4465c9b74a2269 before and after)
    .graphify_extract.json: written (237 bytes)
  ```
- **Other cases, v8:** a fake `graphify` printing 3 lines gives exit 1 and `SyntaxError`; one printing 1 line works, because the line lands inside the comment; no `graphify` on PATH gives exit 0 with `command not found`. A fake `changed` printing 3 lines in the `--update` merge block gives exit 1 and `SyntaxError`, with `graph.json` and `manifest.json` untouched.
- The `# Save scan root so \`graphify update\` ...` lines in Step 1, `shell/posix.md` and `shell/powershell.md` are plain shell comments outside quotes. Checked: a fake `graphify` was not called.

### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Comment text only, in four fragment lines. No stored format changes, and reverting is one commit.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Comments inside Python source the skills hand to the interpreter. Nothing in `graphify/*.py` changes.

- **Cache and ids:** no change. The semantic cache key comes from `prompt_fingerprint`, which hashes the file the skill passes as `prompt_file`, `references/extraction-spec.md` (`cache.py`). That file is not in this diff. aider and devin pass no prompt. No node ids, graph format or manifest change.
- **Generated files:** 60, all regenerated with `--bless` and never hand-edited: 16 monoliths and 14 `references/update.md`, plus their 30 `tools/skillgen/expected/` copies. `skill-windows.md` is one of the 16. Its text changes, but it was never affected, because its Part C sits in a single-quoted PowerShell here-string (`@'`).
- **`gen.py`:** one line. `_is_semantic_origin_stamp_fix_line` matched the Part C comment with its backticks, so the round-trip audit would reject the new text. It now matches the text without backticks. The old string is not needed: the pinned v8 baselines for aider and devin hold neither form, and `--monolith-roundtrip` passes.
- **Open PRs, checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree` against each branch's head, then the new test run on the merged tree:**

  | #4313 | clean | 163 passed |

  | #4371 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4434 (at 75218d94) | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4452 | clean | 163 passed |
  | #4456 | clean | 163 passed |

  - #4344 and #4353 spell the opener `"$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)" -c "`. The test accepts both spellings, so it runs on their merged trees as well.
  - #4434 added a comment with backticks inside a `-c` block (`core.md:208`). Its branch now drops them too (75218d94), so the new test passes whichever lands first.
  - #4456 can later drop the PATH filtering at `tests/test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py:156-160`, which exists because of this bug. Not changed here.

### Not covered

- The runtime check runs only `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."` statements in fenced bash blocks (quoted or not). Other shapes, such as `"$PYTHON" -c "..."`, are not run; the static check still scans them.

## What does this PR do?

Part of #4447: this fixes the aider and devin skills only. The 14 generated hosts are fixed by #4313, and this PR does not touch that file (`tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md`) or any generated `references/update.md`.

**Merge order:** independent of #4313. Either can land first, and they touch different files. #4313 fixes the 14 generated skills, this PR fixes aider and devin. Once both are in, I'll add the 14 skills to this PR's test so all 16 are covered.

### Summary

On a code-only `--update` the aider and devin runbooks said "run only Step 3A, then go straight to merge". Part A writes `.graphify_ast.json`, the merge reads `.graphify_extract.json`, and nothing wrote it. Part C would write it, but it reads `.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally, and in these two files the Part B fast path is prose only.

```text
aider / devin skill, code-only path

 --update, "If code_only is True"
-  run only Step 3A, go straight to merge
+  Step 3A (AST) -> Part B fast path -> Part C -> merge

 Part B, "Fast path:"
+  block writes an empty .graphify_semantic.json     (Part C reads it unconditionally)

 only-deletions guard (aider only)
-  writes graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json        (the aider merge reads ./.graphify_extract.json)
+  writes .graphify_extract.json

 commit 2 (separate bug)
 --update section
+  block writes .graphify_detect.json from .graphify_incremental.json
   (Part A reads it, Step 9 deletes it, nothing in the section wrote it again)
```

Three commits:
1. `fix(skill): aider and devin code-only runs reach the merge (#4447)`: the paragraph, the fast-path block, aider's guard path, the test, and the `gen.py` audit entry for these lines.
2. `fix(skill): aider and devin --update populate .graphify_detect.json`: a separate bug found while testing. Fixes #4455. Without it Part A fails first after any full build. It can be dropped without affecting commit 1.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4449.

When a JS file and a file with another extension share a stem in one folder (`x.mjs` plus `x.sql`) and the `.mjs` declares a variable named like the sibling's extension (`const sql = ...`), the `.mjs` file node ends up labelled `sql`. `graphify explain "x.mjs"` finds nothing.

`extract()` renames each file's old file-level id (its path with the extension: `esquema_x_sql` for `esquema/x.sql`) to the canonical one (`esquema_x`). It did that on every node, edge endpoint and raw call that spells the string, whichever file it belonged to. The JS variable `sql` is minted `{stem}_{name}`, which is also `esquema_x_sql`. So it was renamed too, salted next to the file node, and dedup dropped one of the two.

This PR renames a key only for the file that minted it, and only when another file's own symbol carries the same id. Every other key renames exactly as before.

```diff
 extract.py, the id_remap pass          (key esquema_x_sql -> esquema_x, minted by x.sql)

   node   sql           (x.mjs)  id esquema_x_sql
-    renamed to esquema_x         (its file did not mint the key)
+    kept as esquema_x_sql

   edge   contains  x.mjs -> sql        endpoint esquema_x_sql, source_file x.mjs
-    renamed: now x.mjs -> x.mjs, a self-loop
+    kept: still points at the sql variable

   edge   imports_from  x.mjs -> x.sql  endpoint esquema_x_sql, target_file x.sql
     renamed (x.sql minted the key), then salted onto the x.sql file node

   edge   imports  main.pas -> util.pas   (no target_file, main.pas holds no such node)
     renamed, as before
```

A key is contested only when a node of a different file carries it as one of that file's own symbol ids. For a contested key, an item is renamed if its file minted the key, kept if its file holds a node with that id, and renamed otherwise. Which file an item belongs to: a node, its `source_file`; an edge source, the edge's `source_file`; an edge target, the `target_file` stamp if there is one, else the edge's `source_file`; a `raw_calls` `caller_nid`, the record's `source_file`. Paths are compared resolved. Swift extension `nid`s and Objective-C field-table keys follow the same rule.

The later `ext_id_remap` pass already has an ownership guard (`owned_ids`, from #2231 and #2243). The first pass lacked it.

### Before / after

The issue's repro, `graphify extract . --code-only`:

```text
before:  [graphify] note: node 'esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x' was extracted twice from 'esquema/x.mjs'
         under different labels (keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs').
         5 nodes, 4 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | sql          <- should be the file node "x.mjs"
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t

after:   no note.   6 nodes, 5 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | x.mjs
         esquema_x_sql           | sql
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t
```

Tests, `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`:

```text
before fix:  8 failed, 6 passed   (the 6 are guards that must not move)
after fix:   14 passed
```

The same cause hit other pairs. Each is a test:

- `x.ts` + `x.css` (`export const css = ...`): `css` took the file node's id, and nothing was salted because `x.css` has no nodes.
- `x.js` + `x.js.map` (`const js_map`): the variable was renamed to the id of `x.js.map`, a node that does not exist.
- `x.py` + `x.sql` (`def sql()`): the function was lost and its `calls` edge started at the file node.
- `x.swift` + `x.sql` with `struct sql` and `extension sql`: without the Swift hunk the fix would delete both file nodes, so the hunk is required, and a test covers it.

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. Reverting is one commit.

**Blast radius:** narrow. The rename changes only for a key that a node of another file also carries as its own symbol id; every other key takes the old path.

- **Ids:** a corpus with no such clash gets the same ids as before. An affected corpus gets its swallowed symbol back under its own id, with its edges. An unchanged affected file keeps its old state in an existing `graph.json` until it is re-extracted.
- **Caches and skills:** the semantic cache key, the AST cache and the generated skill files do not change. `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts` and similar are never in the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`).
- **Cost:** one extra pass over `all_nodes` before the rename loop, dictionary lookups and memoized path resolution.
- **Open PRs:** none of #4344, #4353, #4371 touches `graphify/extract.py`.

### Not covered

- The Objective-C hunk has no test that reaches it. I could not build a case where an Objective-C class node holds a contested id. It runs only when some key is contested (`if contested:`), and the 5 existing objc tests pass with it.
- Unstamped cross-file imports to a same-stem file (for example Pascal `uses util` next to `util.js`) already end on a node that does not exist after salting, with or without this bug. A contested key now behaves like an uncontested one there. That dangling edge is not repaired.
- A symbol named like its own file's extension (`const js` in `x.js`, `def py()` in `z.py`) is lost. The same file owns the key, so this rename fix does not touch it. It needs its own issue.
- Stub nodes: I scanned graphify's own repo and its test fixtures for a node whose file did not mint the key. The one hit is `sample` in `tests/fixtures/sample.lpk`, a Lazarus unit reference minted with `sample.pas`'s old id. Before this fix it collided with the lpk's own file node; now it keeps its own id and its edge follows. Other languages and extractors were not scanned.
- Through `graphify extract .`, only siblings of a supported type (such as `.sql`) trigger the bug. `collect_files` skips `.css` and `.map`, so those two pairs need an explicit `extract([...])` call.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a symbol is never renamed because of a file it does not belong to, and everything that refers to a file node still ends on that file node.

- The issue repro runs with relative and absolute paths: three distinct ids for the file node, the variable and the `x.sql` file node.
- After `build()`, the labels `x.mjs`, `sql` and `x.sql` all exist.
- With `import raw from "./x.sql"` in `x.mjs`: `imports_from` ends on the `x.sql` file node, `contains` and `calls` end on the variable, and there is no self-loop.
- An unstamped Pascal import on a contested key ends exactly where the same edge ends with no clashing variable.
- Controls from the issue (`const db`, `const sql = 1`, no sibling, a sibling with another stem), and a Lazarus stub from a different stem, keep their ids.
- Gating only the node rename, and leaving edge endpoints on the old id-only rule, was tried and does not work: it leaves a `contains x.mjs -> x.mjs` self-loop and a `calls` edge that starts at the file node.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4432. #3103 reported the same thing and was closed without a fix.

The extraction prompts say node ids use "only `[a-z0-9_]`". `graphify/ids.py` keeps Unicode letters. For a path like `docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md` the model cannot follow both, so it invents a stem, and the stem differs between chunks and between runs. `_semantic_id_remap` only strips stems it already knows, so none of them get fixed.

This PR states the real rule and gives the model each file's stem, computed in code.

```diff
 graphify extract (llm.py)
-  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="...">
+  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="..." stem="docs_tz_лз4">

 skill, Part B
   check_semantic_cache(...)
     writes .graphify_uncached.txt              # unchanged
+    writes .graphify_uncached_stems.txt        # path<TAB>stem, same order
   Step B1: FILE_LIST lines
-    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md
+    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md<TAB>docs_tz_лз4       # falls back to the old file if missing

 rule text (llm.py + both extraction-spec fragments)
-  Node ID format: lowercase, only [a-z0-9_], no dots or slashes.
+  Node ID format: lowercase. Letters and digits of any script are kept as written
+  (never transliterated to ASCII); every run of any other character becomes one _.
+  ...use the given stem character for character as the id prefix.
```

Both paths use one new helper, `file_id_stem(path, root)` in `graphify/extractors/base.py`. It returns `make_id(_file_stem(...))` of the root-relative path. The skill computes the stems in the same Python step that already runs the cache check. No path is pasted into code, and no agent types a stem.

I left `_semantic_id_remap` alone. A made-up stem has no known length, so a repair can't tell where the stem ends and the entity begins. The #4281 prototype also showed that re-keying a node from its `source_file` moves a node that mentions another file under the wrong file.

### Before / after

Same id, two different stems:

```text
before:  ids.py stem      docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог
         model's stem     docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog            (from the issue; changes per run)
         remap            {}                                      (nothing reconciled)

after:   prompt carries   stem="docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог"
         page node id     docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог   (same string, tested)
```

Read literally, the old rule turns that path into `docs_tz_4_`. That result comes from running the rule as code, not from a model run.

Tests, `tests/test_unicode_id_rule.py`:

```text
before fix:  43 failed, 2 passed   (the 2 are the host-count guards)
after fix:   45 passed
```

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. The only new file is a temp file that Part B cleans up, and reverting means one commit.

**Blast radius:** medium. Every semantic extraction prompt changes:

- **Cache:** the semantic cache is keyed on the prompt text, so every existing entry misses once. This hits `graphify extract` users and all 14 skill hosts, including ASCII-only repos. Reverting causes one more miss.
- **ASCII paths:** the chunk prompt is byte-identical apart from the added `stem="..."` (tested). File-node ids do not change for any path.
- **Skill hosts:** 14 hosts get the regenerated skill and spec. Aider and devin are not touched. They never stated the `[a-z0-9_]` rule.
- **#4344:** one-line conflict. Both PRs touch the same `check_semantic_cache` line in `core.md`. Whichever merges second changes `root = 'INPUT_PATH'` to `root = read_scan_root()`.

### Not covered

- Nothing enforces the id. The model can still ignore the stem it is given, and then ids drift as before. Enforcing it means having code mint the ids, which is a larger change.
- Nodes with no file stem at all (`concept_*`, `s301_totals` in the issue).
- On the skill path, a symlinked doc whose target is outside the scan root gets no stem and falls back to the rule text.
- The aider and devin monolith skills.

## Type of change

## Verification & Invariants

- `test_file_id_stem_is_the_prefix_the_pipeline_mints` runs a Cyrillic and an ASCII document through the real `extract()`. The page-node id equals `file_id_stem`, the chunk prompt carries that stem, and `_semantic_id_remap` leaves a node under it alone.
- `file_id_stem` is tested with an absolute path and root `"."`, with a path outside the root (returns `""`), and with `"`, `<` and `>` in the name. The stem holds only letters, digits and `_`, so it cannot break out of the attribute.
- The Part B step is extracted from the generated `graphify/skill.md` and run. It writes the expected `path<TAB>stem` lines, with `INPUT_PATH` substituted once.

## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Fixes the misleading warning the reporter hit.

When two files mint one id, dedup keeps one node and merges the other into it. The warning claimed that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity", for every such collision. On the reporter's corpus that was wrong: none of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. They were one entity described in two documents, or a reference to another file, and merging them was correct. This PR rewords the warning to say what the merge did. It does not change which node survives.

```text
_report_id_collision(nid, survivor, loser)        # cross-file branch only
  survivor defines the id, loser does not  -> silent          (unchanged)
  head = "kept <survivor> from <file>, merged <loser> from <file> into it"
  if _defines_id(survivor) or _defines_id(loser)
    "the id comes from a file path: either a reference to the kept file (merge is right)
     or a separate document (its own label and attributes are lost; edges stay)
     -> advise 'graphify extract' per subfolder"
  else
    "the id comes from neither path: probably one entity described in both files"
```

Edges stay on the kept node because both nodes have the same id. What is dropped is the merged node's own label and attributes.

Real stderr, before and after (both from `deduplicate_entities`):

An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. The id comes from a file path, so the merged node is either a reference to the kept file (then the merge is right) or a separate document (then its own label and attributes are lost; its edges stay on the kept node). To keep separate documents apart, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.

```diff
-[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
+[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
```
